Pair Programming: Two students work together on programming tasks, with one coding and the other reviewing, followed by role reversal.
Project-Based Learning: Students develop a complete responsive website by integrating HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and backend technologies.
Problem-Based Learning (PBL): Object-oriented concepts are taught through real-world programming problems that require analysis and solution design.
Peer Code Review: Students review and evaluate each other's object-oriented programs using structured evaluation rubrics.
Mini Application Development: Students design and implement Java-based applications integrating multiple OOP concepts and GUI features like AWT & Swing.
Simulation-Based Learning: Solving LPP and Transportation Problems using Python simulations and visualizations.

mentoring.description:
I am mentoring the M.Sc. Data Science students of the 2022–2027 batch. As part of the mentoring process, I conduct weekly counselling sessions for 10 students to understand and address their academic, personal, and other concerns.

Students are encouraged to feel free and comfortable in sharing their difficulties, including issues related to studies, personal matters, hostel facilities, and hospitality, with special attention to the concerns of girl students. I provide appropriate guidance and support based on their individual needs and assure them that their concerns will be treated with care and confidentiality.

Students are motivated to communicate their problems without hesitation, and necessary remedial measures are initiated as soon as possible in coordination with the concerned authorities. This mentoring approach helps create a supportive environment that promotes students' academic progress, well-being, confidence, and overall development.

valueAdded.particulars:
This course focuses on the principles and application of software design patterns to develop reusable, flexible, scalable, and maintainable software systems. It covers object-oriented design principles, SOLID principles, creational, structural, and behavioral design patterns. Students learn to identify recurring software design problems, select appropriate design patterns, and implement effective solutions for real-world applications.

Key Areas Covered: Object-Oriented Design, SOLID Principles, UML, Creational Patterns, Structural Patterns, Behavioral Patterns, Refactoring, and Practical Pattern Implementation.
Course Outcome: Students will be able to analyze software design problems, apply suitable design patterns, and develop modular, reusable, and maintainable applications.

Course Scope:

This course focuses on developing mobile applications using cloud-based backend services. It covers user authentication, database management, cloud storage, APIs, push notifications, and real-time data synchronization. Students learn to integrate backend services into mobile applications for secure, scalable, and efficient application development.

mentoring.description:
Regular mentor–mentee interactions were conducted to monitor and support students in their academic and professional development. The following mentoring activities were carried out:
1.	CAMU Course Enrolment: Guided students in CAMU course enrolment and provided timely reminders for completing the enrolment process.
2.	Fee Payment Remiander: Provided reminders regarding semester/course fee payment and important deadlines.
3.	Academic Performance Monitoring: Regularly monitored students’ attendance, CAT marks, mark sheets and overall academic performance.
4.	SkillRack Support: Addressed SkillRack-related issues and monitored students’ coding practice and progress.
5.	Placement Training: Monitored students’ participation and progress in placement training programmes.
6.	Placement and Career Guidance: Provided guidance regarding placement preparation, career opportunities and skill requirements.
7.	Scholarship Support: Shared information about available scholarships and guided eligible students in the application and document-submission process.
8.	Support for Academically Weak Students: Identified students requiring academic support and provided counselling, guidance and regular follow-up.
9.	Online Certification Courses: Encouraged students to enrol in and complete NPTEL/SWAYAM and other relevant certification courses.
10.	Internship Guidance: Guided students in identifying and applying for suitable internship opportunities.
11.	Technical and Skill Development: Encouraged students to participate in technical events, workshops, hackathons and skill-development programmes.
12.	Individual Mentoring and Follow-up: Addressed individual academic and administrative concerns and coordinated with the concerned faculty members/departments whenever required.

innovativeMethods.method: SketchUp Plugin Exploration (Self-directed & Peer Learning): Students were assigned to independently explore a SketchUp plugin of their choice, study its features and workflow applications, and present their findings to the class, encouraging self-directed learning and peer-to-peer knowledge sharing. Outcome: A compiled reference manual on plugin applications was developed from the student presentations, benefiting all 40 students in the course.

Housing Documentation (Case-study & Field-based Learning): Students undertook detailed case study documentation of housing precedents, including site surveys and mapping of existing conditions, analysis of the case studies, documentation of stakeholders' contributions, and formulation of design proposals responding to the identified housing needs. Outcome: Students developed practical skills in case study analysis, stakeholder engagement and design proposal formulation, benefiting 40 students.

Hands-on Experience on Live Site (Experiential / Field-based Learning): Conducted a live, on-site demonstration as part of the case study exercise, giving students first-hand exposure to real-world construction practices, spatial organisation and site conditions. Outcome: Students gained practical, first-hand understanding of construction and site practices, benefiting 30 students.

innovativeMethods.method:
MICRO TEACHING METHOD:............................ This technique has been adopted for the design subject to teach certain “drawing based” inputs. During the session an A0 size hardcopy print out of the particular drawing is placed on a table and student group of “10 students only” are called for discussion surrounding the AO size drawing sheet.
The drawing details are explained in detail to that specific group and the teaching method has been found to be very effective. That is the teaching contents are strongly absorbed by that specific group and it encourages very interactive “doubt clarification” sessions as well , students ask doubts more freely as the group is very small.
For a class strength of 40 students this session has to be repeated 4 times, thus it is time consuming but very effective to explain even very “complex ideas” and “drawing based ideas” in a very effective manner.

ON SITE TEACHING METHOD:.................During august 2025 students were taken to a construction site “ALLIANCE – URBAN RISE” ( a 20 floor high rise apartment in Chennai.).  in the site of this live ongoing project , various construction details and architectural aspects have been demonstrated in a very live manner for direct understand of students. This session was conducted by myself along with expert architect Ar.Ramapriyan.

coursesDesigned.remarks:
Preamble  
This course introduces the essentials of New Product Development (NPD) with a focus on 
product certification, global regulatory frameworks, and pre-compliance testing. It covers key 
international standards, electrical disturbances, and EMC/EMI requirements, along with 
protection techniques for Surge, EFT, and ESD. Students will also learn harmonic sources, 
effects, and compliance under IEC 61000 standards to support reliable and certifiable product 
design.

This course provides a fundamental understanding of power quality issues, harmonic control, 
and EMI/EMC requirements in electronic systems. It focuses on filtering methods, power 
factor correction, and harmonic measurement instruments, along with key EMC standards 
and noise coupling mechanisms. The course also emphasizes practical design techniques 
for EMI/EMC compliance and familiarizes students with standard testing procedures and 
measurement environments.

The objective of this course is to provide a comprehensive understanding of optical 
communication systems and networks. This course provides coverage of basic optical 
technology including physical aspects of light propagation, fiber optic components and its 
characteristics and modulation/demodulation techniques and link design. It also covers 
enabling technologies for optical network including SONET/SDH, WDM network, integrated 
optics and photonics, future optical systems and Networks.

The course on Real Time Systems is designed as a theory that aims to provide students with 
an understanding of operating system and real time systems principles. This subject dives into 
the core principles and practical applications of the embedded systems in real-time 
environments. The course covers Hard and Soft Real-Time systems, task scheduling, inter 
process communication and other resources managements. The final stretch of the course is 
covered with practical examples that showcase Free RTOS in action, and its API use cases

coursesDesigned.remarks:
Syllabus
Crystal structures:
Basic terms-types of crystal systems, Bravais lattices, miller indices, d spacing, Atomic packing factor
for SC, BCC, FCC and HCP structures, X-ray diffraction methods to determine crystal structure.
Structure, properties and selection of engineering materials: Classification and properties of Materials- Metals and Alloys, Polymers, Ceramics, Composites & Semiconductors(Elemental and
Compound). Selection of Materials for Engineering applications.
New Materials -Super Conducting materials - Smart materials – Nanomaterials- High temperature
materials, Nuclear Engineering materials, Metallic glasses, Fiber optic materials, Super strong
materials, Cermets, Display materials, Thermoelectric materials, Electrets, Surface Acoustic Wave
Materials, Bio materials.
Imperfection in solids and strengthening mechanism: Point, Line, Surface and Volume defects,
Dislocations and plastic deformation, Mechanisms of strengthening: solid solution strengthening,
strengthening by Grain Size Reduction, Recovery, Recrystallization, and Grain Growth, Strain
Hardening and Precipitation Hardening.
Mechanical Property characterization: Tensile Test (UTM) -Young’s modulus, True stress and strain,
Engineering stress and strain, Stress-strain curves, Generalized Hooke’s law, Yielding and yield
strength, Ductility, Resilience, Toughness. Hardness: Rockwell, Brinell and Vickers and their relation to
strength.

innovativeMethods.method: Under the flipped classroom model, design concepts, procedures, and benchmark problems were discussed during class. Higher-order design problems were assigned for self-learning, and their complete solutions were reviewed in subsequent sessions. Supporting PDF materials and solved examples were provided through Google Classroom to facilitate independent learning and reinforce design competency.
Complex steel structural systems and design details were explained through model demonstrations, enhancing students' visualization, conceptual understanding, and application of design principles.

PTC Mathcad was utilized as a modern computational tool during classroom sessions to demonstrate steel design calculations, enabling students to verify intermediate and final results, understand design procedures, and improve computational accuracy.

PowerPoint presentations integrated with relevant video resources were used as ICT-enabled teaching tools to enhance conceptual understanding, visualization, and student engagement during classroom instruction.
Think-Pair-Share was practiced in the classroom to promote collaborative learning, encourage active engagement, and sustain meaningful student-teacher interaction.

coursesDesigned.remarks:
This course is designed to help students develop a comprehensive understanding of the key
concepts, attributes, and types of urban infrastructure and their significance in planning
processes. It examines the status of infrastructure in India and its influence on social and
economic development, while exploring strategies for planning, designing, and managing
systems such as water supply, sanitation, solid waste management, social infrastructure, and
transportation. The course also covers relevant standards, guidelines, and regulatory
frameworks that govern urban infrastructure development and highlights the critical role of
planners in promoting sustainable, efficient, and inclusive infrastructure solutions for cities.

This course enhances the students' understanding about urban information systems and
helps them to learn advanced techniques to analyze the configurations. Students are also
introduced to urban configurations, spatial analysis and GIS which help them to analyze
complex cities easily with the help of tools. The course aims to equip students with the
analytical tool necessary to understand the urban configurations and plan the urban
environments.

innovativeMethods.method: Students were divided into five stakeholder groups: City Police/Administration, Informal Vendors’ Association, Residents’ Welfare Association (RWA), Municipal Authority, and Tourism & Local Business Council. The debate theme was: “Should cities legalize and promote night markets for informal workers despite challenges of safety, zoning and neighbourhood opposition?” Each group prepared its position using the National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM) street vendor component, the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014, and the case studies of the Bangkok night markets and the Connaught Place Night Bazaar proposal in Delhi. Groups argued from their stakeholder’s viewpoint and responded to the others. The session ended with the class working out a negotiated, balanced position on regulation, zoning and safety.

Harveypatti, Madurai was allotted as the study neighbourhood, and student groups were formed by infrastructure sector: social infrastructure and physical infrastructure (water supply, electricity, etc.). Each group surveyed its sector in the neighbourhood, compared the survey findings with the prescribed norms, identified the gaps, and proposed measures to fill them. The sector-wise findings were then brought together to give a combined picture of the neighbourhood’s infrastructure.

Problem-Based Learning (PBL) – Applied Microeconomic Analysis and Urban Policy Design: Students analyse a real-world urban issue in an Indian city using microeconomic concepts such as scarcity, demand -supply, elasticity, consumer behaviour, welfare economics and market failure. They formulate evidence-based policy interventions and assess their economic effectiveness and social equity.

studioPedagogy.outcomes: Case study report, base map with analysis overlays, existing land use map and SWOT analysis, vision statement, concept plan, zoning plan and road hierarchy diagram; LAP and TPS layout plan, street sections, built form diagrams, public space design drawings and infrastructure schematic ; feasibility study, draft regulations, and final LAP report .

Weeks 1–4: topic selection, literature review, research design and proposal submission. Weeks 5–8: primary and secondary data collection, ethical considerations and interim findings report, followed by Review 1. Weeks 9–12: thesis structuring, maps, graphs and diagrams, and draft submission. Weeks 13–16: revision, final proofreading and thesis submission, followed by Review 2 (thesis defence).

The students were encouraged to simulate their design solutions in tools like, sketchup, climate consultant to analyze the climate responsive design features incorporated in their design which is beyond their studio's objective. The actual neighborhood issues of Madurai's major slum (Melavasal & Thideer Nagar) were studied, and design interventions were made at both neighborhood level and building level  and presented to the community and a NGO who is involved in the slum's redevelopment projects.

The course adopted a combination of experiential learning, software-based simulations, performance analysis to enhance student engagement. Students undertook daylighting simulations using digital tools to visualize illumination distribution and evaluate environmental performance. Hands-on acoustic assessment exercises involving reverberation time calculations enabled the application of theoretical concepts to real spaces.  These approaches promoted analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and the integration of environmental and technological considerations in architectural design.

Students visited the Civil Engineering Department laboratories and gained hands-on experience with material testing equipment. coursesDesigned.remarks:
Introduction to Embedded Systems
Definition and characteristics of embedded systems – Classification – Design metrics – Application domains – Processor, memory and I/O organization.        
Embedded Hardware Design
Microcontrollers, DSPs, SoCs and ASICs – Memory devices – Sensors and actuators – ADC, DAC, timers, watchdog timers – Communication interfaces. 
Embedded Software Design
Firmware architecture – Device drivers – Interrupt handling – Scheduling concepts – State machine based design – Embedded C programming.
Communication Protocols
UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, USB, Ethernet – Protocol selection and implementation. 
Design Methodology and Optimization
Requirement specification – Hardware/software partitioning – Power-aware design – Reliability and fault tolerance – Case studies.

Embedded Processor Overview
General purpose processors- Microcontrollers - DSP processors - Application specific processors 
ARM Cortex Architecture
Architecture - Registers- Instruction set - Assembly programming - Memory map - Exceptions and interrupts - Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller (NVIC)
RISC-V and Advanced Processor Architectures
Architecture - Reduced Instruction Set Computer-V - Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) - Comparison with ARM - Open-source ecosystem
Processor Interfacing
GPIO - Timers - PWM - Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) - communication peripherals - Programming
Performance Optimization
Pipelining - Cache - Power management - Benchmarking

Introduction to Machine Learning
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning concepts – Types of learning – Data preprocessing – Feature engineering – Training and testing datasets – Model evaluation basics.
Supervised Learning Techniques
Linear regression – Logistic regression – Decision trees – Support Vector Machines – Random Forest – Classification and regression applications.
Unsupervised Learning Techniques
Clustering – K-means algorithm – Principal Component Analysis (PCA) – Dimensionality reduction – Association rule mining.
Deep Learning Fundamentals
Artificial Neural Networks – Activation functions – Backpropagation – Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) – Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) – LSTM networks.
AI Applications and Case Studies
Computer vision – Natural Language Processing – Predictive maintenance – Fault diagnosis in electric vehicles – Smart grid analytics – Industrial AI applications.

valueAdded.particulars: Internet of Things (IoT) refers to things that can be connected to internet and can send or receive data through internet for sensing/monitoring and/or control purposes. IoT consists of combination of Hardware and Software. IoT systems are used in realization of smart appliances, smart home, smart city, smart grid, smart irrigation and smart transportation etc. Microcontrollers, sensors and/or actuators and communication modules are the major components of IoT system. Programming the microcontrollers in the IoT system is essential to implement the given IoT application. In this course, programming Arduino, ESP32 and Raspberry Pi for various IoT applications is covered.

Design has been defined as a “systematic, intelligent process in which designers generate, 
evaluate, and specify concepts for devices, systems, or processes whose form and function 
achieve clients’ objectives or users’ needs while satisfying a specified set of constraints”. 
Human-centered design is defined as a process and a set of techniques used to create new 
solutions for the world. Solutions include products, services, environments, organizations, 
and modes of interaction. The reason this process is called “human-centered” is because it starts with the people we are designing for. This course facilitates the development of 
students’ professional skills through their team engagement in developing conceptual 
design for a local community problem.

innovativeMethods.method:
Architectural Thesis—· Radiation-Based Form Development: Students were introduced to ArchiWizard to analyze solar radiation and tested multiple building massing options by varying orientation, geometry, curvature, and form configuration. 
· Performance-Based Design Iteration: The radiation analysis outputs were used to identify solar exposure patterns and iteratively refine the building form, integrating the optimized form into plans, sections, and the final thesis proposal. Beneficiaries: Architecture thesis students and faculty benefited through improved integration of computational analysis, sustainability principles, and evidence-based design decision-making into the architectural design process.

Architecture principles—World Architecture: Narrative Travelogue Portfolio: · Students select significant architectural case studies for each unit and document them through a structured Narrative Travelogue Portfolio using sketches, diagrams, photographs, and written narratives. 
· Students analyze each case study through form, geometry, spatial organization, and spatial relationships, connecting their observations to architectural principles and personal interpretation.

Vertical spanning system—Students were made to explore the concept of using different structural systems and components (curtain wall, stud wall, and roof systems) for the same plan layout using two different materials: R.C.C. and steel. Structural system and material usage for varying heights—IV Yr B Arch
Students developed an understanding of structural system selection, material behavior, and construction components by comparing RCC and steel systems across varying building heights

mentoring.description: Remedial mentoring was conducted for 9 students of T’SEDA during the 2025–2026 Odd Semester to support their academic improvement in subjects where additional assistance was required. Individual subject-wise faculty in-charges were assigned to guide students through structured remedial sessions. The process included an initial discussion on 27 August–05 September 2025, follow-up reviews on 01–08 September 2025, and final submission of written assignments or mock tests by 15 September 2025. The mentoring covered CRA, Design Thinking and Principles of Design, HSS, Materials and Components, Site Planning and Site Services, and VSS.

studioPedagogy.outcomes: Public Space Mapping	21AR161 - Fundamentals of Design Students were taken to a public space, and they produced maps for linking the spaces in sequence, identity, and perception with an understanding of activity, time, behavior, place attachment, etc., using principles of abstraction.	I Yr B.Arch - · Students explored planar interaction, transformation, and three-dimensional form development through hands-on paper-folding exercises.

Students applied radiation analysis to assess solar exposure and heat gain, using the results to develop and refine climate-responsive building forms and orientations. 
CFD analysis was introduced to evaluate airflow, wind movement, and natural ventilation, enabling students to incorporate performance-based strategies into their studio designs.  -   Outcome: Students developed the ability to use radiation and CFD analysis to make evidence-based decisions for energy-efficient and climate-responsive architectural design. 
· Beneficiaries: Architecture students and faculty benefited through improved integration of environmental performance analysis, simulation tools, and sustainable design strategies into the studio process.

innovativeMethods.method:
21AR331 - HORIZONTAL SPANNING STRUCTURES 
1. Hands-on Structural Learning (Interdisciplinary workshop with Civil Engineering Department)  : Students prepared analytical sheets on horizontal spanning systems and their structural components. An interdisciplinary workshop with the Civil Engineering Department was conducted to provide practical exposure. 

2. Google form assessment (MCQ)
A Google Forms MCQ assessment was conducted after Unit 2 as a formative assessment to identify conceptual gaps and reinforce learning.

21ARPP1 - PLACEMAKING 

1.Role play based problem solving 
Students were divided into groups and assigned real-time urban and public-space issues. They enacted role-plays representing different stakeholders such as users, authorities and other affected groups to understand conflicting perspectives. Students subsequently prepared presentations identifying the problem, stakeholder concerns and possible design/planning solutions. 

2.Proposal for the real time problem 
Continuation of the Assignemnt 1, Students gave solutions /  proposals for the Real time issues taken.

21AR220 - CLIMATE RESPONSIVE ARCHITECTURE 

1. Joint teaching studio was conducted in collaboration with Ar. Lilly Rose, SPA Vijayawada. 

2.Digital Simulation 
The collaborative sessions introduced students to Climate Consultant software and other climate-analysis tools, along with topics aligned with the course plan. Students interpreted climate data and explored its relationship with architectural design strategies.

studioPedagogy.outcomes:
1. Case Study 
Students were taken for a real-time case study to observe residential spaces, spatial organization, scale and user requirements. They developed physical models to understand residential scale, proportion and spatial relationships, followed by student presentations explaining their observations and design interpretations.

Simulation softwares for lighting, Ventilation & Climate responsive design. 
Students were introduced to ArchiWizard to analyse solar radiation and tested multiple building massing options by varying orientation, geometry, curvature and form configuration. 

3.Performance-Based Design Iteration: 
The radiation analysis outputs were used to identify solar exposure patterns and iteratively refine the building form, integrating the optimized form into plans, sections and the final thesis proposal.

studioPedagogy.activityName: Informal settlement Planning and design along with heat mitigation strategies
studioPedagogy.outcomes: The studio enabled students to understand the complexities of low-income housing redevelopment through field-based learning, community engagement, analytical mapping, and design exploration. Students developed skills in identifying urban issues, applying different planning and design theories, integrating climate-responsive strategies, and translating site analysis into housing and neighbourhood-level design proposals.

The studio adopts an experiential, observation-based and inquiry-driven pedagogical approach, encouraging students to understand architecture through direct engagement with the built environment. Through an on-site farmhouse case study, students investigate spatial organization, functional zoning, circulation, climatic responsiveness, materiality, construction techniques and the relationship between built and natural environments. Structured activities such as freehand sketching, sensory mapping, spatial documentation, user interaction and architectural detail studies promote critical observation and analytical thinking. Students are encouraged to interpret how architectural spaces respond to user needs, environmental conditions and contextual characteristics. The learning process integrates observation, documentation, analysis and design interpretation, enabling students to translate real-world spatial experiences into informed architectural design decisions.
